Study exercise derived from this source. Explain the approach in your own words, work through an example, and identify edge cases. For code, implement your own version and discuss its time and space complexity.

#include<cstdio>
#include<vector>
using namespace std;

class Solution {
public:
    int singleNumber(vector<int> &nums)
    {
        int bits1 = 0, bits2 = 0;
        for (int num : nums)
        {
            int bits1_new = 0, bits2_new = 0;
            for (int i = 0; i < 32; i++)
            {
                int hi = (bits1 >> i) & 1;
                int low = (bits2 >> i) & 1;
                int sum = (hi * 2 + low + ((num >> i) & 1)) % 3;
                bits1_new += (sum / 2) << i;
                bits2_new += (sum % 2) << i;
            }
            bits1 = bits1_new, bits2 = bits2_new;
        }
        
        int res = 0;
        for (int i = 0; i < 32; i++)
        {
            res += ((bits2 >> i) & 1) << i;
        }
        return res;
    }
};

int main()
{
    Solution sol;
    vector<int> nums = { 0,1,0,1,0,1,99 };
    printf("%d ", sol.singleNumber(nums));
    return 0;
}
